Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. This is the final call for Flight four five seven to Paris. All passengers should now be at gate twelve. We will be closing the gate in ten minutes. Passengers with a connecting flight to Lyon, please note: you will be going through passport control in Paris, not in Lyon. If you are traveling with a carry-on bag, please place it in the overhead bin, wheels first. Our cabin crew will be serving dinner about one hour after takeoff. During the flight, we may have some turbulence over the Atlantic, so please keep your seatbelt fastened when you are in your seat. Thank you for flying with us, and have a pleasant flight.

I fly to Europe for work four or five times a year, so here is my routine for a long-haul flight. The night before, I check my baggage allowance on the airline website. An excess baggage fee at the airport is always more expensive. I get to the airport three hours early, because the line at the security checkpoint can be very long. After security, I go straight to the lounge and answer my emails. So while other people are running to the gate, I will be relaxing with a coffee. On the plane, I drink a lot of water, I sleep a little, and I change my watch to the new time zone. Why? Because when I land in Europe, I won't be going to a hotel to rest. I will be walking into a meeting. So I plan the flight as part of the work trip.

First, I check my baggage allowance on the airline website the night before. Then, I get to the airport three hours early and check my bag at the counter. Next, I go through the security checkpoint with my carry-on. After that, I wait in the lounge until the final call. Finally, I board the plane and find my seat.
